body.heading: Where in the world is Senegal?
paragraphs: Senegal is a country in Western Africa, which is part of Africa.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Senegal is Dakar.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Senegal speak Wolof and French. Wolof is the language you will hear in markets and homes; French is the official language of school and government.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Senegal is the West African CFA franc. The CFA franc is shared with neighbouring countries, so the same money works across the region.

body.heading: How big is Senegal?
paragraphs: Senegal covers about 197,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of Zimbabwe.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: A short ferry from Dakar, car-free Gorée Island has pastel streets, bougainvillea and the House of Slaves museum — a moving place to learn history together.
Lake Retba really is pink! Tiny algae turn its salty water rose-coloured, and workers harvest salt in white piles along its shores.

body.heading: Think and talk

2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?
